title: 2026-11-30 Model Gatekeeper & Pin Validation Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review sandbox run results, decide on a candidate model pin, and agree on rollback/fallback rules. Customer concerned about regression risk and cost; Redwood suggested a quantized fallback plus canary gating tied to error and latency SLOs. Agreed next steps: run 50k token benchmark across v1.2 (baseline), v1.3-beta (candidate), and q2-small (quantized fallback); SE to share benchmark sheet and config; security to review KMS/SAML docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 09:27 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Sophia (Redwood SE), Dana (BlueHarvest Head of AI), Eric (BlueHarvest Platform), Priya (BlueHarvest Security)

[00:00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call, then we'll go straight into the sandbox results.
[00:00:12] Dana: Yep, Dana here. Thanks.
[00:00:15] Eric: Eric on the call.
[00:00:18] Priya: Priya here.
[00:00:21] Marco: Marco from Redwood. Sophia as well.
[00:00:30] Ava: Great. We'll start with the summary of the internal runs — Marco, do you want to walk through the heatmap and the tradeoffs?
[00:00:37] Marco: Sure. So we ran the scheduled 3-model benchmark across the 48-hour window you gave us. The models were v1.2 baseline, v1.3-beta (candidate), and q2-small-ops which is the 4-bit quantized fallback. I put the sheet in the shared folder: "bench/blueharvest/11-30". Quick takeaways: v1.3-beta improves average handle-time by ~15% on your instruction set but has a tail latency increase at 95th pct, about +120ms. q2-small lowers cost ~40% per token but increases token-level hallucination risk on our evals, so quality dip especially on your long-context summarization tests.
[00:01:30] Dana: When you say hallucination risk, can you give an example from the eval set?
[00:01:34] Marco: Yeah, so on the clinical note summarization set there were multiple cases where diagnoses were compressed and a few false assertions were introduced. Not catastrophic but above your current acceptability threshold in the rubric. Some of that is prompt rework though — we saw that stronger system prompts recover a lot of the degradation.
[00:02:05] Eric: Latency-wise, our SLA is 300ms p50 and 500ms p95. Where do these models land?
[00:02:12] Marco: On your dev region hardware (A100-ish dedicated hosts), v1.2 hits ~220ms p50, 380ms p95. v1.3-beta: 190ms p50, 500-520ms p95 (so borderline on p95). q2-small: 160ms p50, 320ms p95. The p95 for beta spikes correlate with long sequence KV cache misses — the tail happens more under synthetic concurrency bursts.
[00:02:50] Priya: And for the quantized fallback, is there any change to encryption or logging? Our compliance team needs to know.
[00:02:58] Sophia: No change to at-rest encryption; models are still in the same KMS-protected buckets. The quantized variant runs on the same infra but uses a different kernel path; audit logs and request tracing remain intact. We will include a KMS key alias mapping in the docs we share.
[00:03:20] Ava: On the customer risk side, we proposed a pin to v1.3-beta for the canary 10% traffic with automatic rollback triggers tied to error rate and quality delta. Dana, is that still your preference?
[00:03:31] Dana: We like the throughput gains but worried about the p95 drift and summarization regressions. I'd prefer a narrower canary — maybe 3-5% — with a slower ramp. Also want explicit manual kill switches.
[00:03:45] Marco: Absolutely — we can do 3% initial canary, step to 10% only after we clear the regression evals on your prompt set over a 24h window. We also recommend enabling prefix cache warming so the p95 tail reduces for similar session patterns.
[00:04:06] Eric: Can you explain prefix cache warming — I saw it in the docs but want practical impact.
[00:04:11] Marco: Sure. It's basically pre-seeding the KV cache for frequent cold-start prompts, so instead of every new session cold-starting the attention state, we push cached prefixes based on user cohorts. That reduces tail latency at the cost of memory. For your usage patterns (many repeated templates), it brings p95 down ~80-100ms in our tests.
[00:04:40] Dana: That's interesting. Memory growth — do we need to change autoscaling?
[00:04:45] Marco: Minor scaling bump on the dedicated pool, yes. We can translate that into cost delta in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:04:52] Priya: On the rollback triggers — what exactly are you proposing? Error rate threshold? Quality scoring? Latency?
[00:04:58] Sophia: Proposal: three parallel gates — automated rollback if (1) error rate increases by >0.5% absolute, (2) p95 latency breaches 600ms for more than 5 minutes, or (3) aggregate quality delta on the eval prompt set worsens by more than 2% measured via your rouge/qa pass metrics. Also manual rollback via console with an immediate cutover to pinned fallback.
[00:05:29] Dana: The >2% quality delta — will that pick up the kinds of hallucinations we saw?
[00:05:33] Marco: It should catch large shifts. For precision on hallucinations, we also recommend a short active anomaly test that samples 200 requests/hour through a scoring function that checks entity fidelity — that's more targeted than aggregate rouge.
[00:05:51] Eric: Who owns that scoring function? We need to integrate into our CI.
[00:05:55] Ava: Redwood can provide a starter scoring harness, but BlueHarvest should own labeling and thresholds. We'll hand off the harness + example configs.
[00:06:05] Dana: Ok. Let's talk about pin semantics — if we pin to v1.3-beta, do we pin the model ID only or the quantization/profile as well?
[00:06:14] Marco: You can pin at multiple granularity levels. Options: model artifact hash (strict), model version tag (semver), or model+profile (e.g., v1.3-beta+q2). We recommend pinning to model version tag and separately to an operational profile for production. That gives you flexibility to adjust compute settings without implicit model changes.
[00:06:39] Priya: From security perspective, pinning the artifact hash is better for auditability — but operationally heavy.
[00:06:45] Sophia: Right, artifact hash ensures exact reproducibility but it forces a full redeploy for any kernel/infra change. Many orgs choose model-tag pin + KMS + deployment audit to get a good balance.
[00:06:58] Dana: Could we do hybrid: pin tag in prod, but keep artifact-hash snapshots in our records and enable quick swap if we detect regression?
[00:07:07] Marco: Yes, Redwood supports a freeze snapshot set that bookmarks artifact hashes per tag; you can trigger a swap to a previous artifact hash instantly via the API. We'll add example commands to the runbook.
[00:07:20] Eric: About the catalog comparison — are there any other model variants we should consider beyond the three? We've seen mentions of a 'safety-tuned v1.3' in the catalog.
[00:07:28] Marco: There's v1.3-safety which has extra fine-tuning for hallucination suppression. It trades some terse accuracy for fewer hallucinations. On your medical prompts it reduced false assertions by ~35% vs q2-small but cost and latency are closer to v1.3-beta. It's worth a small focused run.
[00:07:50] Dana: Let's include safety-tuned in the expanded benchmark.
[00:07:53] Ava: Good. We'll do four models then.
[00:07:56] Priya: On compliance, we need to confirm SSO/SAML, audit log retention, and encryption for test artifacts. You gave some docs earlier but our security team flagged missing KMS usage examples.
[00:08:06] Sophia: We'll send the KMS examples and a sample retention policy mapping. For SAML, Redwood supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; we can do a SAML test in your staging next week.
[00:08:18] Dana: Next week is tight — maybe the week after.
[00:08:22] Ava: Noted.
[00:08:24] Marco: Back to fallback runway — we propose the following roll-forward/roll-back policy: nominate q2-small as the runtime fallback pinned to a stable artifact hash; pin v1.3-beta as candidate tag with canary at 3% -> observe 24h -> step to 10% if pass -> 48h observation -> open to 25%. At any point, console kill or the three gates auto-cut.
[00:08:52] Eric: If we cut back to q2-small, will we still serve the same prompt formatting? I want to avoid needing prompt changes mid-flight.
[00:08:58] Marco: The API surface is identical; however output characteristics differ slightly. We recommend a small output-normalization layer (post-processing) for token-level fixes — we can ship a starter sanitizer in the harness.
[00:09:12] Dana: That helps. How long to run the expanded benchmark? We're concerned about sample size — your earlier 48-hour run was useful but we want statistical confidence.
[00:09:21] Marco: For robust p95 and quality estimates we recommend at least 50k tokens per model on real traffic distributions or a 7-day window if you run synthetic bursts. Given your request, 50k tokens per model will be our minimum.
[00:09:34] Priya: Can Redwood run that on our dedicated pool? Or do we need to schedule capacity?
[00:09:38] Sophia: We'll coordinate with your infra team. It should be fine on the dedicated pool; if you want to avoid impacting production we'd recommend doing the runs in a staging pool we provisioned which mirrors your config.
[00:09:50] Eric: Staging pool sounds right. We'll make a capacity slot next Thursday morning.
[00:09:56] Ava: Great. Quick check on metrics collection — do you want Redwood's built-in latency+cost breakdown or do you prefer raw logs to ingest into your own observability?
[00:10:07] Dana: Both. Send the Redwood breakdown and exportable CSV.
[00:10:11] Marco: Will do.
[00:10:14] Ava: Ok, let's move to explicit next steps and owners.
[00:10:18] Ava: Marco, you'll run the expanded 4-model benchmark (v1.2, v1.3-beta, v1.3-safety, q2-small) and share the results sheet and config.
[00:10:26] Marco: Yep. Target: deliver bench results within 5 business days after we get the capacity slot.
[00:10:31] Ava: Sophia, you'll produce the rollback runbook and the CLI snippets for artifact hash swap and pinning.
[00:10:36] Sophia: Yep. I'll include the console screenshots and the kill switch steps.
[00:10:40] Ava: Priya and BlueHarvest will confirm the SAML/KMS acceptance criteria and give a go/no-go for canary percentage.
[00:10:47] Priya: We'll review, target a decision in 3 business days after receiving the KMS examples.
[00:10:53] Eric: I'll provision the staging capacity next Thursday.
[00:10:56] Dana: Also, can you include a suggested canary timetable in the runbook — step timings and expected observability windows?
[00:11:02] Marco: Yes, included.
[00:11:05] Ava: Any other risks or items we didn't cover?
[00:11:08] Dana: One more: cost forecasting for the tagging/pinned vs fallback scenario — we'd like a 6-month spend projection under 3 adoption curves.
[00:11:16] Marco: We can produce conservative, expected, and aggressive spend models. I'll add them to the bench sheet.
[00:11:22] Priya: And please flag any components that require HIPAA data handling adjustments — though we are testing on de-identified data, our legal team wants to see the mapping.
[00:11:30] Sophia: We'll annotate the data-flow diagram and KMS mapping for that.
[00:11:34] Ava: Great. Quick recap then close.
[00:11:37] Ava: Agreed actions: expanded 4-model benchmark, run in staging, bench sheet + cost model, rollback runbook and CLI snippets, KMS/SAML examples, sample anomaly scoring harness.
[00:11:46] Dana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:11:48] Marco: Thanks, we'll follow up with the sheet and a proposed schedule.
[00:11:52] Sophia: Bye.
[00:11:54] Priya: Thanks.
[00:11:56] Eric: Bye.

Note: transcription contains a few mis-hearings (e.g., "sam-el" or "K V cache" for KV cache) and occasional overlapping talk that the auto-transcript resolved as best effort.
